name: Ruadán

attributes.attribute: was the cause of the desolation of Tara
condemned Ruadán for hiding a relative accused of murder

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: In Irish legend the hero Ruadán brought about the fall of Tara. The account ties that ruin of the great central hill to him, long the chief seat of politics and belief in the land. Tara's king Diarmait condemned him for sheltering a relative who faced a murder charge. In reply, Ronán laid a curse on the king and on Tara itself. From that time on, Tara never again held the strength it had in Celtic times.

okr.objective: Present Ruadán and the curse that dimmed the power of Tara.
key_results: Ruadán was the cause of Tara's desolation.
Tara was the old political and spiritual capital.
King Diarmait condemned him for hiding a murder suspect.
Ronán's curse lessened Tara's strength from then on.
okr.evidence: Monaghan, Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore
